title: Giant Defy Vs. Specialized Roubaix SL8 | Which Is The Best Endurance Road Bike?

takeaways.text: BikeRadar tested the Roubaix SL8 Expert at £6,000 (US$6,500) with SRAM Rival eTap AXS, Roval carbon wheels and an alloy bar and stem.
The Expert uses Future Shock 3.2 with fluid damping and springs but no adjustable damper, which is reserved for the S-Works and Pro; set in the middle, it never felt too soft or too hard.
A deep aero seatpost replaces the old flexible post; frame and fork clear 40 mm tires, with mudguard mounts front and rear, a third bottle mount under the down tube and top-tube bento mounts.
Quick steering and an active front end let it carry speed over bumps, potholes and gritty corners, helped by tires that spread to nearly 34 mm.
The ride is split between a smooth front and a firmer rear: on bigger bumps the rear takes the edge off, but on smoother roads it feels noticeably stiffer at the back.
BikeRadar found it versatile and comfortable with a great turn of pace, but a bit hefty and less agile than the Defy, and picked the Defy overall.

disclosure: BikeRadar's senior technical editor rode both bikes; the video does not say how they were supplied.
summary: A November 2023 comparison of the Roubaix SL8 Expert with the Defy Advanced SL 0; the takeaways cover the Roubaix only. The Expert shares the FACT 10r SL8 frame with the Sport 105 recorded here but has a higher build and a different Future Shock version.
